title.narrative: FAO - Building Resilience in Middle Shabelle (BRiMS)

description.narrative: BRiMS projektet kommer bidra till att öka motståndskraften hos utsatta människors försörjning till matosäkerhetskriser genom att hantera de bakomliggande orsaker till sårbarhet i Middle Shabelle, Somalia. Fokus området i BRiMS projektet har utsatts för återkommande torka och översvämningar. Bristen på befintlig och fungerande bevattningsinfrastruktur, utbredd osäkerhet och tillgångsutmaningar är andra utmaningar i Midle Shabelle som hämmar jordbrukarnas produktion och resulterar i försvagad motstråndskraft hos befolkningen. I ljuset av de senaste, återkommande torka och översvämningar, är den huvudsakliga fokuset på detta projekt kring vattenfrågor och bevattning: främst tillgång till vatten samt dess förvaltning.

The project will substantially increase the resilience of vulnerable people’s livelihoods to food crises by addressing key underlying causes of vulnerability in Middle Shabelle, within Somalia’s breadbasket. The area faces recurrent drought, flooding, non-functioning irrigation infrastructure, widespread insecurity and access challenges that impede farmers’ production, related supply chains and market potential. In light of recent, recurrent drought and flood emergencies, the main vulnerability addressed by the project centres on water: primarily water access, management and its productive use.

title.narrative: FAO BRiMS Decision on Amendment 4 of Contribution

description.narrative:
Rehabilitation of irrigation canals and embankments increased access to irrigation water, enabling 62% of households to expand cultivated land and contributing to significantly higher agricultural production among beneficiary households. Programme participation was associated with an average increase of 416 kg in harvested produce and 0.27 hectares of cultivated land.
Improved irrigation, training and input support contributed to increased crop production. Around 60% of BRiMS households reported higher production than before the project, and 94% reported increased income from crop sales.
Farmers adopted improved agricultural practices. Use of certified seeds was higher among BRiMS beneficiaries (46% in Phase 1b compared to 25% in the comparison group) and over 70% of households attributed production gains to BRiMS training and extension support.
Capacity development led to behavioural change among farmers. Seventy-one percent of trained farmers applied new knowledge and skills and 68% shared knowledge with others. More than 90% of farmers applying IPPM practices reported increased crop yields and reduced pest damage.
The project strengthened local institutions. Eighty-six percent of respondents reported that BRiMS supported the formation or strengthening of farmer groups, while water user associations improved coordination of water distribution, maintenance and conflict resolution.
Disaster preparedness improved. Sixty-three percent of households received early warning information and 64% adopted disaster risk reduction measures such as embankments, safe grain storage and livestock protection.
Food security improved among beneficiary households. BRiMS households achieved better Food Consumption Scores than comparison households, and Phase 1a households recorded the highest Resilience Capacity Index, indicating stronger resilience through improved productive assets, adaptive capacity and social networks.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
